chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

had a lot of fun writing this one. i locked in and wrote most of this in one sitting which is kind of wild to me!! hope you all enjoy!!

Two days after waking up from his very sudden, tantrum-fuelled coma Phainon called the trailblazer.

More specifically, it took two days for his call to be answered. Not that he was trying particularly hard to contact her. When his first attempt at calling - using the word 'attempt' was extremely loose, considering he wasn't even the one controlling the teleslate - got him sent through to voice mail, he'd simply deemed the entire thing a waste of time and proceeded to bury his head into his pillow until Mydei sighed and gave up.

The next day when Phainon used his own teleslate to call, Stelle picked up on the first ring as if she'd been waiting for him.

He tried not to think of all the negative reasons she might have been waiting and instead fiddled with the sleeves of his new coat from where it had become a permanent fixture in his lap. Mydei had likely mentioned the reason for his call the day before and she'd known they would try to get into contact again. That was all.

It was a video call; Stelle only ever answered video calls. She'd once explained that it was necessary if she was going to take screenshots of all her friends and add them into March 7th's photograph collection. Apparently, she even had a secret video call photo album or whatever that she kept hidden behind the fake Sparkle bomb she kept on her sofa.

(Or at least, Phainon thought the Sparkle bomb was fake. He also remembered something about fireworks? Or that the dolls had been hiding bombs? He couldn't remember and he also did not care enough to ask for clarification.)

The screen flicked to life and from Stelle's side of the galaxy Phainon was greeted by the Trailblazer's forehead and a single lock of grey hair falling across skin that he was pretty sure had gone unbrushed since the Astral Express had left Amphoreus.

"Heeeeeeey buddy!" Stelle said. "How's it hanging Sunshine?"

Phainon stared at her forehead for approximately three and a half seconds before closing his eyes and letting out an extremely long-winded sigh. He said, "I thought I was babygirl. Why am I now Sunshine?"

"Why?" He heard muffled movement and when he checked moments later, Stelle had moved back from the camera just enough to also see her eyes and the bridge of her nose. He resisted the urge to sigh again. Even when she wasn't physically present it felt like she wasn't abiding by the rules of personal space. "Well because you light up my world, partner. 10 out of 10 stars. Wait— no. You're the OG sun. Sunshine premium."

Usually when she lost him to her rambling, Phainon simply smiled politely and nodded. He would tell himself that he didn't really need to know and that if he really wanted to know then eventually the World Wound Web would explain it all for him. But right now, all he really felt was irked by the fact that in all the time he'd known these guests from beyond the stars, he had only understood about half of what Stelle had ever said. It shouldn't have been so difficult to understand whatever the fuck it was she was talking about. And yet.

"Right," he said, unimpressed.

"Oof," Stelle said with a wince. "Tough crowd. No being silly with the silly bean, gotcha. Okay Phai-boy, if you're more in the mood for seriousness instead of some lighthearted teasing then that's fine too. I can totally be serious, you know I—"

…This was the true Deliverer of Amphoreus? Really?

He cut her off. "Mydei said you were worried and I should call to check in."

Stelle shuffled back from the screen and he could finally see her in full. The first word that came to mind while looking at her was frazzled. She looked a few steps closer to the raccoon photos she'd shown him in the past that accompanied messages of '#me' or '#raccoongoals'. Heavy bags had collected under her eyes; She looked like it'd been a while since she'd slept through the night in full.

Alright, maybe he didn't like seeing a worried trailblazer. She didn't look suited to worry. It made him concerned.

"I have been worried! You haven't checked in with me in so long I was starting to get all jittery like some poor bride jilted at the alter!"

Phainon's gaze lifted past his teleslate to Mydei who was currently stood at the nearby counter removing pomegranate seeds from segments of cut fruit and placing them in a small container. Sensing the sudden attention directed his way, Mydei turned and gestured towards the seeds.

Phainon shook his head — food was still as much the enemy as crockery — and asked, "How long was I unconscious for?"

"Eight days."

Turning back to where Stelle was trapped in his screen, Phainon said, "It's not even been two weeks."

"I was still worried! But that's not what's important right now. Are you like… okay?" Phainon's eye twitched; He was really beginning to hate being asked that question. "Okay. Clearly you're not but like... I heard about what happened and I guess I wanted to check in on how much fire there is in the room right now?"

He had to resist the urge to sigh. The past few days hadn't done much to temper the anger in his chest and as such, the fire that Stelle was referencing was very much still burning. It was honestly surprising how his mind hadn't crumbled away entirely with how much it clung to his blood. At least it helped him sleep - being angry was exhausting.

"A lot," Phainon said and watched Stelle wince again.

"Yeeeeah," she said. "I kind of figured it would be after talking with Cas and Cyrene, they both—"

He cut her off again. "I don't want to hear anything about Cyrene for now. She's—" The edge of his teleslate sizzled. He forced a deep breath in and out. "I'm trying to be calmer but if we talk about her then I won't be."

Stelle blinked. "That's actually really emotionally aware of you."

Phainon scowled.

"I mean it in a good way!" Stelle continued, flapping her hands in front of the screen as if the action offered further clarity - (it didn't) - before he could even ask what the hell that was supposed to mean. "Just— We'll talk about something else. Mydei's with you, right? What did you think of the playlist I sent him for you?"

"It was…" New. Unfamiliar. A relief after lifetimes of the same fucking thing grinding against his eardrums. "…Alright."

"Only alright? Was it too peppy for you? I heard you liked Robin's music so I was going along with that vibe but maybe you need something a little more grunge. Or more punk rock?"

Phainon had literally no idea what she meant by either of those things so he simply nodded his head aimlessly and resisted the growing urge to hang up on her.

"Sounds great," he said.

"We can listen to it in person when we're back!" She said it like a promise, as if she were expecting it to be soon and for Phianon's mind to still be a functional thing instead of an even more decayed mess than it already was. "Oh! I'll get both March and Dan Heng to make you a playlist too. We'll have a sing-a-long session and all that jazz. Or just a Lo-Fi hangout depending on what you're feeling. It'll be so fun!"

It didn't necessarily sound fun. It sounded like it'd be more of a bother than anything. Knowing Stelle, she'd probably turn the music on too loud and be obnoxious about literally everything while he suffered through the experience of pulling her away from every single trash can she could feast her eyes upon. The idea sounded like a chore.

The bitterness was clawing its way into his bloodstream again and Phainon closed his eyes so that Stelle wouldn't be able to catch it swarming him. Hopefully, the call wouldn't pick up on the way his already poor mood was starting to plummet further.

No. He told himself. No. Stop it.

There was literally no reason to be frustrated with the Trailblazer of all people. No reason for his flames to target her. After everything he really was grateful for all of the aid she and the Astral Express had brought. She'd delivered them into the Era Nova, for titan's sake! She was the true hero of Amphoreus. She was!

He was so endlessly grateful for that and not even a little bitter about it because there was no point in being bitter.

But… when she acted so carefree and thoughtless…

…Well, it felt a little insulting to realise that she had managed what he could not.

"Yeah, I'll tell them to make the best playlist," Stelle continued, oblivious to his inner monologue. "It'll give us all something to do during our warps. They're always so boring."

Phainon peeked an eye open. "You're heading back so soon?"

"Yeah! We set off a few days ago, actually. We've got to make a few stops for the geniuses because they want to pick some stuff up but we should be back in a couple of weeks!"

Phainon blinked. Once. Then twice.

Then, he lifted a hand to the bridge of his nose and pinched the skin as hard as he could. He could see Mydei in his peripheral vision watching him closely, weighing up whether he needed to keep him from hurting himself but the ruling was evidently no need.

"I thought you were busy at the space station?"

"Sure was! But then you did your timey-wimey magic and shit changed. Which— that was super rude of you by the way, I got trapped in the simulated universe breaking vases for forever. It sucked!"

Something rough caught in Phainon's throat. "I didn't realise people would notice."

Stelle's brows pinched together in thought. She said, "I don't think many people did. Oh, but Herta and Screwllum definitely noticed. They were trying to do set calculations to see how much distance the time loop covered but so far they've not been able to find the edge of that space. That's wild. Who knew you were so strong. Herta really wants to speak with you. She and Screwllum are coming back with us so they can say hi. It's why we're coming back sooner!"

Phainon frowned. "Remind me who Herta is?"

"She's one of the Genius's that helped us fight against Irontomb." The name was familiar so he'd expected that Herta would've been one of the Expresses allies. They'd delivered the remains of the Scepter to her too, if he was remembering correctly. But he'd wanted a different context. Stelle had specifically mentioned her own relationship with this genius during the cycles and he couldn't clearly remember what she had told him about her. Something about being an assistant? He wasn't sure. "I guess you never actually met her during the cycle we experienced with you, she and Screwllum only really showed up after the Flame Rea—Well. They only showed up at the very end, anyway! Cyre—"

Stelle paused, realising that she had neared a landmine. She cleared her throat.

"Anyway! They're the ones I do tests for in the Simulated Universe."

…Ah.

Something dropped inside of his brain. It clattered into the silence and sounded like clarity. Phainon moved his new coat from where it sat in his lap and placed it on the counter beside him as his expression flattened. He could feel the warning shocks of something close to calm but not bubbling inside of him. They were like harmonic tremors acting as a signal. Though for what, he wasn't entirely sure.

"Herta wants to talk to me?" He repeated. "Why?"

Stelle shrugged. "Oh. Well, I reckon she's just a little interested in what you can do. Or, er— okay, maybe she's a lot interested in you. And the fact that apparently you're enough of a bamf to turn back time for a huge amount of space."

Didn't the Geniuses follow the Erudition? They were all scientists following Nous, right?

And Nous was the Aeon that Lygus had wanted dead. Nous was his…

…Failed creation?

His lips pressed together and Phainon's forehead crinkled with such force that the lines left in his wake were downright cavernous.

"Your scientist friend is interested in me?"

Stelle waved the comment away with a hand. "Well, I'd hardly call Herta a friend but—" She glanced at him from the corner of her eye and froze. Her lips opened and closed, as if realising what she had just said, as if suddenly understanding that his sudden calm was not actually calmness at all but an impending eruption of emotion. She stuttered, "No! I mean— I mean yes. But. In like, a totally and completely ethical way, really, so—"

His expression soured. He could feel flame burning against his vision and was vaguely aware that the rising burn of coreflame must've dyed his irises with gold.

"Your scientist friend," he breathed, "who makes you run simulations over and over inside of a coded universe—"

Stelle winced. "That's really not—"

"—finds me and my abilities interesting enough to pause her other research and come to Amphoreus." He felt something crack inside of his lungs and realised that it had been caused by a dramatic increase in the temperature of the air surrounding him. "She wants to study me, doesn't she?"

"No! I mean, not really. Maybe a little." Stelle lifted her hands in surrender. "That's 100% not what I meant though. You know that's not what I meant! She'd never force you, it's totally all up to you!"

She was bringing a scientist back with her to Amphoreus and that was— that was bad. He couldn't do that again. Be studied. Be inspected and analysed for every error within his code, to be bugged and debugged and copied and deleted and, and—

'̴̲͌Ţ̴̎͝ĥ̴͈i̶̯̓s̴̪̄ ̵̣̹̄w̴̫̭̃á̸̘̗̓s̶̢̰̎̇ ̸̢͑ȁ̷̧ļ̴̼͠ẃ̷̰̣̏ą̸̳͋̅y̷͇͗̀s̴̝͌ ̴̪̀t̵̨̙̉̑ȟ̴͉̺͌ẽ̷̲̒ ̶̢̞͊d̸̦̒ȇ̵̤ś̸͚̾t̷̛͖ỉ̷̺͓̒n̶̛͉̗ ĕ̷̩̥̩̥d̶̰̕ ̶̭̀̓ę̵̇̅ń̵͔̱̀d̷̦͘͝ ̶̬͌̕ṭ̸̀̐ṏ̷̗ ̶̟̃ö̴̱̔u̵̒ ̠̳͊r̷͇̈́ ̵͙̚g̵̢̕͜͜ a̸̧̳̓m̷̝̆ḙ̸̘̒̈.̴̘̼̍̉ ̶̰̺̉I̷͈͆t̴̃ ̗̭̍ ̸̻̅c̷͋ ̣̜̈́o̸̲̿u̶̹̲̎l̷̠̹̐d̸̺́̐ ̵͔̯̽n̶̛͈̪͋e̸̛͇̅v̵̪̞̌͠e̷͚̱̔̀ ŕ̴̺̀ ̷̙̠̊b̴͚̥̏̓ẹ̴̺͒̌ ̵̮̰͠ä̷̗͕́̕v̷̙̍o̷̦̪̐̕i̸͍̓d̵̪̩͂e̵̪͖͋d̷̢̀̎.̷͖̑'̵̹̏

—No.

"Tell your Genius Herta," Phainon hissed, "that I would rather slit my own throat— no, better yet, permanently delete my code from the system, again — then have her be even remotely interested in me."

"Partner—"

Phainon didn't snarl at the teleslate in his hand but that was not out of restraint. It was because one moment it was a teleslate and the next it was nothing more than scrapped junk. His fist closed with such force that the device crunched and buckled beneath his strength, a mess of concaved metal parts and cracked glass.

His lips curled. His chest heaved from the onslaught of destruction pooling in his lungs like smoke and— and speaking of smoke, he was pretty sure that he was burning. Again. And bleeding. Again. His hand dripping gold, gold, gold, and his code rippling in such a way that he could tell that it was infected with something, some sort of virus. Some—some sort of remnant of Irontomb, probably, or a fail safe installed into him by Lygus just waiting for the right trigger.

"Ph—non!"

Mydei's voice felt too far away for him to focus on.

He knew, objectively, that losing his temper here was a risk. With each passing day he could feel the steady return of energy into the coreflames, the rising heat, the blazing power. And he knew, he did, that being angry in this state had led him to destroy so much. Even within the Era Nova. He'd ruined Aedes Elysiae. His room. He'd burned bridges with Cyrene, even if it had been her fault.

And yet, he couldn't calm himself.

There was something echoing in his ears like a siren call and it made him want nothing more than to break things. To melt the scraps of metal in his hand, to burn down this stupid fucking hospital and all the wires inside of it, to just give in to all of his anger and rage and—

He couldn't stop it. It wasn't just about whether he wanted to or not. He— Phainon wasn't sure he physically could.

A rattle echoed on his lips. It sounded like Destruction. Enticing. He snarled again and launched the fragments of his teleslate at the wall.

"P—" Something grabbed hold of his shoulders and jerked him forwards. The movement was so sudden it made his thoughts shake. "Phainon!"

…Wait. What was he—

Phainon blinked and there was Mydei, nails digging into his shoulders with such pressure that the force left him breathless.

"Calm down," Mydei said, and he looked… Phainon wasn't sure if it was fear or worry in his eyes but there was something primal there. "Copy my breathing. In. And out."

"Why?"

Why should he?

"Just do it," Mydei repeated. "With me. Inhale."

Phainon inhaled.

"Good. Now, exhale. As much as you can."

And exhaled.

"Yes. Just like that. You're doing great."

And continued to do nothing but breathe until finally Mydei nodded his head, uncurled his fingers and let go.

A shudder wracked its way down Phainon's spine at the sudden absence of pain. Without it to ground him, he could feel the pressure of rage weighing down on him again and he… he needed to be anywhere that wasn't here. Not in this room, not in this goddamned hospital, maybe not, even, in Okhema.

"Mydei," he breathed and it sounded more like a high pitched whine, a plea. "I need— Fresh air. Something. Anything. Just— Just get me out of here." His voice caught in his throat and cracked. "I don't want to be here anymore. Please."

Mydei's lips thinned.

He reached for Phainon's blanket only to hesitate as its the edges crumbled into ash and stained his fingertips. Then, he cast his attention sideways, grabbed hold of yellow fabric and thrust Phainon's new coat into his arms. "Can you walk?"

That was a question he really didn't know the answer to. He'd find a way. Whether he had to use the coreflames or simply drag himself across the ground with shaking limbs he would find a way.

"Of course you can't," Mydei muttered before Phainon could speak. It sounded more like he was speaking to himself. Nodding to the coat, he said, "Put that on. I'll carry you."

Chapter End Notes

chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

we're about halfway through act 2 with this chapter!! i'm quite excited for it. (I wasn't lying when I said this one is the shortest of the acts!!)

hope you're all enjoying the fic. thank you for all of the comments, i love reading and rereading them even if i don't always manage to respond to them!

Mydei did not carry him out of Okhema but they did end up at the city's border.

As if falling back into routines they had once shared, Mydei abandoned the streets in favour of the Okheman rooftops. The buildings at the city's edge were more stable, if not a little dusty from where the wind had swept debris and silt onto flat walkways and into empty gutters. As such, they were able to traverse the roofs with few worries that the surrounding structures would collapse from the smallest shift in weight.

Phainon burrowed as deeply into his coat as he could. In part because the sudden drop in temperature from his smouldering hospital room to the outdoors was enough to leave him shivering and also because he didn't want anyone in the streets below looking up and seeing him in his current state. He didn't want to learn how the civilians of Okhema would react to the sight of his snarling lips or the cut of his glare.

In an attempt to hide from anyone who did glance up he pressed his forehead into the curve of Mydei's shoulder.

"Is the river okay?"

"Huh?"

Mydei's hold of him tightened. It was difficult to know whether it was in response to the dry crack in Phainon's voice or just coincidence. Probably

coincidence. If it were because of him, Mydei wouldn't hold on. He'd have let go.

"I know a place that overlooks the river," Mydei said. "But I don't want to go there if you don't want to."

Phainon was pretty sure that he knew the place that Mydei was thinking of. By the riverside - or rather, on the streets above it - there was a small alcove built into the side of a building nestled in thick ropes of overgrown ivy. In some of the cycles they'd cleared the ivy and reinforced the rotting walls. Then they had used the building as a temporary outpost when travelling back into the city after missions. It had always helped to have a place to rest when they'd been too exhausted to make the trek all the way home to the Marmoreal Palace.

They hadn't repurposed it in his final cycle. Hadn't in the last hundred or so. It was probably still abandoned.

Which made it the perfect place to go to avoid people.

"Phainon?"

"I don't care," he said, the words scraping from his throat. Phainon frowned - that made it sound like he did care, at least a little bit. Which he didn't. He added, "It's fine. The river's fine."

Mydei's chin brushed against his hair as he nodded. "Then we'll go there."

Phainon didn't respond. He was doing his best to keep from thinking too much.

(His best, of course, was not good enough. It never had been.

And so his thoughts spiralled.)

So… The Astral Express was returning sooner than he'd expected they would. Which was a good thing. Or would have been a good thing if their return didn't include an agreement to act as personal chauffeurs to two geniuses. One of whom was interested in him. And perhaps wanted to use

him as a subject in one of her experiments. The idea made his skin crawl. He could feel copper sparks brushing across the bruises of his still healing arms. Even just the thought of Herta's interest sent a rippling wave of revulsion down his spine.

Except… he didn't know for certain that Herta wanted to study him. Not really. Stelle had only said that the woman was interested in the act he had accomplished against time and now wanted to speak with him.

But still…

…And it wasn't as if he didn't trust the Astral Express. He did. Chrysos Heirs withstanding, the Express crew were the group he trusted most. Even if he'd only conversed with two of their current members. He knew their temperament enough to know they held no malice. The Nameless were benevolent. They had saved Amphoreus. They had saved him. Knowing this, it was impossible to truly believe that they'd suddenly flipped personalities and were now trying to ruin his life, readying to throw him back inside of the very machine they'd helped to pry him out of.

He trusted the Express. And if the Astral Express trusted these geniuses, stating that their visit to Amphoreus would not cause any hindrance to their healing planet, then logically he knew that was probably true. They wouldn't bring any harm. There likely wouldn't be any more experiments.

If anything, meeting Herta would include a brief conversation that he'd be able to easily escape by saying 'I'd rather not talk about anything actually, thanks,' without being pushed past his limits.

And really, how self-centered was the belief that they were visiting Amphoreus solely to come and study him? Herta probably wasn't visiting Amphoreus out of interest for him. She and the other one were likely only visiting because they had helped tosave it and wanted to see the planet they'd made such efforts for. Speaking with Phainon was likely an afterthought to their trip.

But still.

It didn't matter that he didn't believe it. Or that it wasn't necessarily rational. The idea had seeped into his thoughts and now, no matter how much he wanted to shake them away, they were there. Phainon knew that it was a long shot. He knew that the probability was infinitesimal. But the truth was that the probability was not zero and so his heart stuttered and his stomach churned and his mind set itself ablaze to protect itself from the influx of fear and icy dread that tried to choke him.

He'd spent eons waiting for the smallest of chances to occur and eventually it had. It made it difficult to trust that this small chance would not find a way to manifest itself as well.

"We're here," Mydei said, effectively dragging him away from the spiral that had left him breathing in rapid gasps. Phainon jerked as he was lowered onto ivy wrapped tiles and cast his gaze on his surroundings.

He'd been correct. Mydei had brought them to the little alcove, though instead of tucking them within the stone alcove they sat at the roof's edge, overlooking the river. It was glimmering a rich cerulean. Water rippled from the fish swimming below the river's surface but from this far away it was impossible to define them as anything more than shadowed specks.

Not knowing what to do with himself, Phainon began picking at the ivy, ripping pieces free. The vines withered and crumbled into ash across his palms.

Mydei sat beside him in silence, legs hanging over the edge of the roof, leaning back on his hands as he half-shut his eyes and tilted his chin towards the sun.

It wasn't an expectant quiet that greeted them and yet Phainon still snapped, "I don't want to talk about it."

"Then don't," Mydei said.

Phainon ripped a bundle of ivy free from where it had started to thread itself in knots around a loose tile in the roof. Pulling the ivy free made it crack in half. His brows furrowed.

"I'm never going to want to talk about it," he continued.

He wasn't sure where his defensiveness had sprung from. Or why he was even speaking. It wasn't like he'd been asked any questions and yet he was speaking regardless.

"That's alright," Mydei said.

Phainon risked a glance from the corner of his eye. The prince was still basking in the sunshine as if he were a lazy chimera. There was little visible tension in his body. (Alright, that was a lie, Phainon could see remnants of it in Mydei's shoulders where the Kremnoan was actively keeping himself from showing his worry.)

The words rose from him like smoke.

"It's just—" He squeezed his hands around the cracked tile from before. Ignored the way it crumbled into dust from the onslaught of his powers. "Is everyone really that fucking stupid? Really? After everything that Amphoreus has been through, did they really think that we'd all be fine with welcoming more geniuses into Amphoreus as if their first society member hadn't caused so much suffering? Amphoreus hardly needs more people studying it right now. It needs—"

He paused. He didn't know what Amphoreus needed. He wasn't entirely sure he was even talking about Amphoreus.

"Not fucking that." He ranted. "It doesn't need that."

Mydei opened an eye. It flicked to Phainon before settling on the patch of ivy between them both. "First society member? You mean the Theoros?"

Despite himself, Phainon flinched away from the title. The cold dread it instilled made him angrier. It was only a title. The fact that a single word could force a physical reaction from him made him want to break something. A lot of somethings.

"He studied Amphoreus," Phainon said, the words pitched high and bubbling forth before he could really think. "He was always watching it. Amphoreus couldn't do anything without him marking it down in his logs. Couldn't do a goddamned thing without him noting the external variables. Without him lamenting another wasted cycle."

Mydei's eyes opened. They settled on Phainon and remained on him. Not studying him but listening. Waiting.

"He— That was how they always ended. With him. With his smug voice and those lifeless fucking eyes. 'Another attempt. Another failure. If history only ever repeats itself, won't you finally end this game?' It never stopped. He never shut up." At this, he turned to Mydei, his heart rattling against his ribcage, his eyes wide. "Mydei, he never shut up."

"Phainon…"

"And it's— See, even if you killed him, no matter how you killed him, Lygus was always there when everything reset. Waiting. Watching. We weren't people. We were just subjects. Code. We were just bugs in a machine that didn't work the way he wanted us to. We were just butterflies and he— he pinned me to the board. He watched me writhe."

Mydei reached a hand out towards him. Hesitated. Phainon turned his head and ripped more ivy from its roots. He tore slabs of tile free and burned fingerprints into the slate.

"Can you imagine if some animation in your teleslate kept fighting against you? That's all we were to him. All I was." Phainon gasped. A laugh caught in his throat and died there. The corpse of it rotted in his lungs and obstructed his incoming breaths. "Wouldn't I catch your interest? Wasn't I fascinating?"

Tears blurred the world. Phainon felt a tremble catch his shoulders.

"And we— we finally got rid of him after… after fucking forever. And now, now, the Astral Express are bringing more of his group here." He lifted his hands and hid his face away. "And they're going to do it again. Because that's just how scientists are. And I thought I— that Amphoreus— was finally free from all of their eyes but I'm not. We're not."

A hand took hold of his wrist and before Phainon could really process it, he was pulled into Mydei's arms.

"That's not going to happen," Mydei said. He could feel the rumble of the words vibrating across the prince's chest.

Heat caught in his blood. Phainon's cheeks were burning under rising indignance. "You can't promise that. You can't."

"I will promise it," Mydei said, evenly. "If the Nameless are bringing those Geniuses into Okhema then we'll just make sure that we are not here when they arrive. We'll take supplies to Castrum Kremnos. Or have Lady Tribbie open a gate for us to Styxia. They won't be able to study you even if they wanted to."

"No." He shook his head with the force one would expect to see in a concussion victim. His brain rattled. "Not Kremnos. I can't— not with you. I can't be in Kremnos with you. Not again."

"Styxia then," Mydei declared. "We'll go to Styxia. If we asked, I'm sure Castorice would show us around."

"Really?"

"Yes. We'll find out the estimated arrival date of the Express and leave before they arrive."

The idea of it was… Frankly it was intoxicating. It included all the fantasy of running away without the subsequent consequences. And maybe the distance would help. He had spent millions of years within Styxia, yes, but nowhere near as many as he had within Okhema. The world had never ended in Styxia. Maybe his blood would cool when surrounded by shoreline and endless sea.

Phainon couldn't believe he was actually considering it.

"Won't it still be empty?" He asked.

"I don't know," Mydei said. "Maybe it will be. Would you not want to go if it is?"

He shook his head. "I don't care either way."

"Neither would I. I don't think anyone we would bring with us would mind either. What do you think? Would going help?"

Would it?

It would certainly lessen the paranoia that the geniuses had brought into existence but it wasn't as if they were solving some sort of historical issue. That worry was a relatively new thing. Or rather, the genius aspect to it was. Running away to avoid a single conversation felt like a disproportionate reaction.

But since when did he care so much about a disproportionate reaction of all things? The cycles had made him act irrationally many times. He couldn't count the number of overreactions or under-reactions he'd enacted during his time trapped within them. Did it really matter? He didn't think it did.

All that really mattered was whether he wanted to go or not.

Phainon took a deep breath. In and out. Then, he pulled himself free from Mydei's arms and met the man's golden gaze with his own.

"Alright," Phainon said. His voice wavered with uncertainty even as he nodded his head. "I don't know if it'd help but… alright. Let's do it."

Mydei's lips lifted into a small, relieved smile. "I'll sort out the details. You'll need to focus on getting your strength back for the trip. Can you do that?"

"Yeah," Phainon said. And it didn't feel an altogether impossible task. Or, at least, it'd be far easier than bearing the fate of Amphoreus upon his shoulders. "I can do that."

chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

as always, thank you to everyone for reading and leaving comments!! i'm always super happy to read through them!! also, at some point recently we broke 7k kudos which is WILD to me?? y'all are crazy. i'm endlessly glad you're all enjoying this fic and my deep-dive into exploring phainon's character.

please enjoy the chapter!!

"Your pegasus is broken."

The words may have been thrown towards Hyacine as she opened the door into his room but Phainon was staring at Little Ica who had claimed his lap as a pillow and had been turning her pudgy chin up in offence at his offering of a honey-soaked wafer. For the last fifteen minutes the little creature had been ignoring the sugary treat as if it had been poisoned.

Obviously it had not.

Little Ica had watched him open the packet that had once housed it. She knew that the food had not been tampered with since Phainon's hands had lifted it out of the packaging. And yet every time he held the wafer out for her, growing increasingly worried and irritated with each passing minute, Ica's beady eyes rolled and she would let out an exasperated nicker.

"She's not broken," Hyacine said in lieu of any greeting.

"Something's clearly wrong with her," Phainon said. He lifted the sweet up so that she could see, clearly, what it was that they were dealing with. Hyacine raised an eyebrow but otherwise looked far less worried than he would've expected for such a dire situation. "Little Ica never turns down food. Little glutton."

"While that may be true—"

"It is. That thing has a problem."

"—there's nothing wrong with Ica. She just doesn't want to take your food."

Phainon narrowed his eyes at Ica. "What's wrong my food?"

Little Ica met his gaze and let out a stern 'doot'. She had clearly learned the tone from Hyacine - It was the tone she used on particularly troublesome patients.

"I think she'd much rather you eat it yourself," Hyacine said.

He scowled and dropped the wafer back into its packet. When even the poster girl for the fucking Voracity refused food from you, it really put things into perspective.

"I'm not going to have it," he said and fixed his most unimpressed look onto the pegasus. Ica blinked. Unaffected. "It's just going to be thrown out."

She still did not take it.

Phainon sighed and, in a fit of righteous indignance, lifted the pegasus from his lap. Then he dropped her onto an abandoned blanket at the far end of his mattress. All very quick. All with very little fanfare.

Letting out a loud whinny, Ica's little eyes filled with betrayal. She whirled her head around to Hyacine - who lifted her into her arms - and burrowed her face into the crook of the healer's elbow until all that could be seen was mane and the edge of her horn. Hyacine patted her mane reassuringly.

"It's not like you to waste food," She said.

Phainon's eyes narrowed and something in his chest fizzled. He was surprised that it wasn't an empty cavity filled only with ashes at this point with how familiar the feeling was becoming. "I'm not. I already told you all that I don't need to eat—"

"Oh," Hyacine lifted her chin to look at him. Her eyes widened. "Oh. No. No. That wasn't aimed at you. I was talking to Ica."

Phainon scoffed and turned his head. "Sure."

"No, really," Hyacine continued, "it was meant for Ica. You already explained—"

"I know," he huffed. It wasn't like he was blind to the fact that he was being defensive and taking the words out of context. Phainon was very aware of the fact that he was being irrational. It was just that the added awareness didn't exactly help to settle him; If anything, it only served to irritate him further. Despite knowing it was the truth, his brain still had difficulty believing it. "I'm just being an asshole. I know you didn't mean it like that."

"Oh. Alright then." Hyacine said.

They fell into what he could only describe as awkward silence until Ica let out a small huff. Then, Hyacine said, "Where's Mydei?"

Phainon jerked a thumb towards the hall. "He's talking Styxia details with Castorice. They were being loud so I kicked them out."

Or… Well, alright, it was less that they were being loud and more that they were talking at all.

He'd woken a little wound up. Again. Lifting his mood back into something sunny was clearly going to be a long-term goal and not an immediate one because most mornings Phainon woke with the overwhelming urge to yell at the sun for daring to wake him. Today he was having a little more difficulty shaking the agitation off.

So when Castorice and Mydei had started talking about the logistics of their upcoming trip and where they could buy adequate camping supplies in a city still struggling to its feet, it had become very apparent that he needed them to get out before he lost his temper.

"Alright," Hyacine said.

He turned back to her. Currently, hesitation bled from each part of her body - from the tighter hold of Ica to the bite of his lip. It had been a permanent fixture in the week and a half since he'd woken from his impromptu coma. Phainon may have apologised for snapping at her upon first waking in the hospital - and for the subsequent times it had happened since - but things with Hyacine had been tense ever since. Or maybe tense wasn't the right word.

Awkward.

Things had been awkward.

It was mostly his fault, he knew that. It was hard to interact with the human equivalent of a pipe bomb. It typically led to a whole lot of worry about when he would next explode. Hyacine wasn't used to being on the receiving end of an anger like this. Especially not his. She wasn't like Mydei, who was used to the burn of war and bloodshed. Nor was she like Castorice, who had dealt with the ire of those she had been forced to execute as the Maiden of Death.

She was just… well, Hyacine.

As a healer, she was used to different types of anger. Bitterness stemming from chronic conditions. The indignance that came from grief? Part of her training included offering a welcome ear to any who needed it.

But this? This all consuming rage that made him shut everyone out, that made him want to tear things to pieces and made him a stranger in his own thoughts?

Hyacine was a doctor, not a psychologist. As much as she tried to understand the emotions simmering inside of him, it was a difficult thing to comprehend in the span of ten days. It was an even harder task trying to figure out a way to help without making everything worse. Hence the awkwardness that had slithered its way into the space between them.

She tried her best to pretend that it wasn't there but it was. And Phainon was too tired to pretend that it wasn't.

A lot of the time he was too tired to even pretend that he wasn't an asshole.

"Are you feeling up to doing some exercises?"

He didn't but Phainon also didn't want to be here when the Astral Express returned so he wasn't willing not to. Instead, he dipped his head in a small nod and let Hyacine take the lead, guiding him through the routine of exercises that she'd put together to help strengthen his muscles and bring him back to something resembling good health.

It was easy to get lost in thought throughout the exercises - and safer too, if wanting to keep his temper in check - so Phainon fell quiet and let himself think.

In the ten days since Mydei had promised that they would leave Okhema for a break, Phainon had taken some time to figure out what exactly it was that he had done to his body by handling time so heavily.

Some things were obvious. By depleting the coreflames he had invited in the cold - his internal temperature had plummeted and hypothermia had sunk in. Cyrene's ice hadn't exactly helped either but that was neither here not there. Hyacine had - in the moments where she was acting more doctor than friend - warned him against depleting the coreflames' energy to such a degree again.

But hypothermia hadn't been the biggest issue.

The biggest issue had been the internal bleeding.

It was difficult to know in full what had caused the backlash with his shoddy understanding of his own powers but time had definitely lashed back. Or rather, it had been the balance of the universe pushing back against him? He'd gone against the flow of existence and whatever kept existence in check had swatted him aside like a bug that was causing more damage than it was worth.

Apparently he was lucky to be alive. The force would've killed most outright but there was something in his golden blood that had kept him alive.

So it seemed he was less of a bug and more of a cockroach.

Castorice, having updated the Astral Express on the situation prior to his waking, had mentioned during one of her visits that the Nameless, Welt, had theorised that it was highly possible that the Equilibrium had caught hold of his meddling and caused his injuries Themself. Apparently time was one of those things They were especially particular about.

Hopefully the theory wasn't based in truth. Phainon was already fed up with the Aeons he'd already encountered.

And regardless, he doubted he'd have encountered another one so soon after the others.

Didn't most of the universe go their entire life chasing Aeons only to avoid their notice? Surely he wouldn't be that unlucky to cross paths with another.

"Yes," Hyacine said, cutting through his thoughts. "That's great. Should we try doing a circuit of the ward?"

Phainon huffed but nodded. "Sure."

Walking was a slow task.

Most things were. Though the coreflames grew stronger with each passing second, the rest of his body still prioritised healing the damage that should've killed him. His body ached and when he walked it trembled with such intensity that Hyacine forced him several times to slide to the floor with his shoulders pressed against the wall until he finally caught his breath.

It was frustrating not having full control over his body. Having it fight against him.

(He was used to it but that didn't make it any less irritating.)

Even if Hyacine took great lengths to remind him that he was healing at an unprecedented speed. To be two weeks into recovery post-coma and already capable of walking on his own two feet was a greater feat than he seemed to think it was. Most people with injuries like him took far longer to walk and, when they did, they didn't manage circuits around the ward. They managed a few steps with the aid of parallel bars.

Oh. And he was still growing the fucking wings. That didn't help with the healing either. It just made the process of healing even more excruciatingly slow.

Today they managed two circuits and a half before Hyacine put her foot down and forced Phainon into a wheelchair. They passed Mydei and Castorice planning as she wheeled him back to his room and, when Mydei offered they come back to keep him company, Phainon glared until the Kremnoan acquiesced and promised that they would come back when finished. Apparently, they would be finished within the quint.

Back in his room - and wasn't it a shame that he was starting to associate this hospital room as being his? - he muttered, "I could've managed three."

"Healing isn't a race," Hyacine replied, helping him back into bed. She reached over to the radio that one of the triplets had left for him, tuned in to some intergalactic broadcast from a nearby star system, and clicked it on. "We only started these circuits a few days ago. You're making good progress."

Phainon grunted, dropped onto his pillow and pulled his blanket over his head.

"I'll let you get some rest," Hyacine said and left him to his news broadcast.

He waited until her footsteps - and Ica's whinnying - echoed into nothingness, then pulled the blanket down from his face and altered his pillow so he could comfortably sit upright. Eyes half closed, he tilted his head back against the pillow and let himself be calmed by a mix of news broadcast and music.

'Hevelius-197's Diamidiata space station, which has seen further expansion following sale to the IPC, will be switching its intergalactic travel restrictions across to the galactic standard from 19th May, 0200 IGST. The Diamidiata space station is responsible for transporting billions of people across Hevelius-197 and, in recent years, has begun to offer intergalactic star transport travel packages. We're here with—'

"Hey Delivery Boy."

Phainon's nose scrunched and he opened his eyes just enough to glower.

"Don't call me that," he snarled.

It was the first time he had seen Cipher within the Era Nova and though he knew he should greet her with some degree of welcome, she'd chosen the worst time to appear from nowhere. Stood in the doorway of his hospital room, her tail swishing in slow, unhurried flicks, she looked nonchalant in a way that only she truly ever managed to be.

She was utterly unaffected by his glare and weaved her way inside towards the cabinet at the far end of the room without a second glance his way. There, she reached for the bag Mydei had brought for his extended stay by Phainon's side. Not even a minute had passed and she was already rifling through Mydei's things as if there would be something of interest inside.

"But you are the deliverer, aren't you?" She drawled and lifted a necklace from the bag. Appraising it, she hummed. "It's what I've always called you. Delivery boy. It suits you."

Phainon's teeth ground with such ferocity that he was pretty sure that he could taste bone. "I am not the Deliverer."

"Oho, look at you getting all riled up." Cipher said. "Let me guess, Gray Mystery is? Sure. She delivered. But she's not exactly our Deliverer, is she?"

"Did you come here just to aggravate me and steal Mydei's things?" Phainon spat.

Cipher raised a brow. "And if I did?"

The blanket in his lap caught fire.

Cipher's tail twitched. Raising her hands in surrender she said, "Easy, easy, you're taking me too seriously. I actually came bearing gifts."

Sighing, Phainon batted at the flames until they died. "…Why does everyone keep trying to give me things?"

It seemed a trend at this point. His memoria blanket from Cyrene - currently folded and tucked away out of sight because seeing it reminded him of how angry he still was at her. The sweater Castorice had made him. The coat from Aglaea. His new radio from the triplets.

Even Anaxa - Anaxa - had send him a droma plushie alongside a note promising that he would not attempt to push Phainon like he had again.

(Mydei had asked him if he was going to name the little plushie to which he had answered that he was not five and thus, would not be. At which point the Kremnoan had smirked and dubbed his plushie 'The Fierce Beast of Kremnos: Kokopo the Fourth'.

Phainon had let him know very quickly that Mydei could fuck off because it was not his dromas to name and that 'Kokopo the Fourth' was just as stupid a name as 'Kokopo the Third.')

"Who cares why? Getting free stuff is always the best, don't you think?"

Unimpressed, he simply looked at her and remained quiet. Once a thief, always a thief.

Like with everything else within Amphoreus, Cipher did not change.

"Anyway, you absolutely want my gift. Trust me. Hold out your hands." When he didn't do so immediately, Cipher clicked her tongue at him and pointed at them. "Go on pretty boy, hold them out."

Phainon raised a brow. "Pretty boy?"

"If delivery boy's off the table then we'll settle for this. Unless you want to be flame boy instead? Though that doesn't have the vibe that I'm really going for. It's pretty boy or bust, I'm 'fraid."

Rolling his eyes, Phainon cupped his hands and held them out. It was better than dignifying her with any response to his new nickname.

Pocketing Mydei's necklace - really, he wasn't surprised - Cipher grinned and sauntered forwards. With a swish of her wrist and a small burst of smoke, multiple pieces of cool rock clacked into his palms. When the smoke dissipated and he looked down, his body stiffened.

In his hands were multiple fragments of golden rock. Old pieces of a mosaic that he couldn't bare to see in one piece. His temperature rose at the sight, instinctual and blazing.

"Are you mocking me?" He asked, voice scraped raw.

"Mm?"

"This isn't a present," Phainon snapped. He jerked his chin towards the pieces of a puzzle that had once been Kephale. "Do you think it's funny to give me this?"

Cipher blinked at him. Once. Then a second time. Before, she'd been grinning but now she was simply watching him without much expression on her face.

"I don't think it's funny at all," she said.

"Then—" His indignance did not fizzle out but it gave way, momentarily, to confusion. She had to have been mocking him. Clearly, she'd seen him that night at Kephale plaza. He'd thought that she was a hallucination but considering how Cyrene had known about his destruction of Okhema's infrastructure, she'd clearly been the real deal. Had it been coincidence that she had seen or had she been following him? "What is this?"

"The pieces of that old mural." Cipher lifted her arms and stretched, arching her back as she did so. Her bones cracked."It was pretty boring going around and searching for pieces of Kephale but here's the fruits of my labor. Pretty sure this is everything. You wanted to destroy this, right?"

He could feel his cheeks burning. A mixture of defensiveness and rage. "I— No. Maybe. What's it to you?"

"Well, I don't exactly like that old thing either." She shrugged. "I did all the work in keeping the Sky Father's lights on for seven hundred years and everyone goes around thanking him for it? Personally, I think this cat deserves her own mural instead. Out with the old, in with the mew."

"What?"

"I'm saying that if you want to burn it or whatever then you should go right ahead. Or, I guess if you don't want to then I'll just go throw them in the sea or something. I know all the best places."

For a moment, he just stared at her.

Then Phainon tilted his chin down and stared at the gold painted pieces of rock in his hands.

He curled his fingers around them and took a deep breath as they started to crumble into ash. Then he said, "I really hate that stupid fucking mural. I have for— for forever."

Cipher hummed. "It must feel good to destroy it."

It was probably awful of him to agree. To admit that he felt good about destroying pieces of Amphoreus' history and that the thrum of destruction caught in his chest each time he broke something to such a degree that it felt satisfying in a way that nothing else did. It was one of those things that he'd expected to keep hidden and locked away for the rest of his life. The kind of admission that showed how truly rotten he'd become after everything. He really ought to keep it a secret.

But he nodded anyway.

His fellow Chrysos Heirs already knew that he was an awful person. There was no reason to try and hide it from them.

"Well then," Cipher said. "If it feels good, then how about we go break some things?"

Chapter End Notes

in case you were wondering, IGST stands for 'Intergalactic Standard Time'. sometimes I just wanna throw random worldbuilding into fics and thus, i gave in to that urge completely. i don't have to kill ALL my darlings. just a few of them.

"i don't have to kill ALL my darlings. just a few of them." - i can see khaslana saying this at least once for the irony. poor guy

Chapter Notes

I really didn't mean to take so long between last chapter update and this one!! But I got pretty unwell with a chest infection and then, while trying to recover from that I moved house. And we only got internet back yesterday so like, here we are.

I've been excited for this chapter and the next one is going to be a lot of fun for me too. We're definitely not too many chapters off reaching the end of Act 2! Hopefully I'll be able to update a little more frequently and complete in the next month or two!!

Thanks again to everyone for reading and leaving comments. I appreciate them all! I hope you continue to enjoy the fic as we continue!! <3

Phainon really shouldn't have been as tempted by Cipher's offer as he was.

But the fact was this: The idea of indulging in destruction was so enticing that he was nodding before he could even think of the possible repercussions. He had no idea what Cipher even meant by 'breaking some things'. For all he knew, she could have been meaning for them to demolish Kephale's statue at Dawncloud.

And really? The shameful truth was that if she had meant that, he wasn't sure whether he would've denied the offer. If anything, the idea was all the more inviting than simple property damage. It almost made him want to agree to her offer more.

The right thing to do in such a situation would be to ask for more details. To learn what exactly Cipher was asking of him and then report to Mydei and Castorice if said offer be handed to him by a poor influence. The right thing would be to sit and wait and have her pitch things to them as a trio. To not be drawn in by the words of a person actively poking at the worst parts of him and telling him that it was time to indulge.

But Phainon hadn't been doing the 'right' thing recently, just the impulsive, and so instead of doing any of that he pointed to the wheelchair that Hyacine had been carting him around in recently and said, "I can't walk too far."

Cipher waved the worry away with a hand. "I'll get us where we need to go. Don't you worry your tired little legs."

A frown furrowed his brows but there was no point in arguing. He was tired.

"All I need is for you to be standing." Her smile sharpened. "You know how my coin works."

He sure did.

All too well. In early cycles, he'd raced her with a coin of his own. (Or, really, it had been re-homed to his pockets from the Ciphera of a previous life). In later ones, he'd used Cipher's own coin to chase her down and rip free the trickery coreflame from her chest.

At this point he was more of an expert on using the coin of whimsy than even Trickery was.

"Yeah," he muttered and began struggling to his feet in an attempt to hide his rising bitterness. "I know how it works."

Standing was difficult. With his strength as depleted as it was, his circuit through the hospital bay had taken most of his energy. It was hard to pull himself up onto both feet, his legs unresponsive and his arms so, so tired, but between the support of his bedside cabinet and the lowered rails of his hospital bed he managed. Didn't even collapse. Which was nice.

And throughout it all Cipher simply waited. There was no offer to help him to his feet. She did not watch him with worried eyes or start chewing on her lip in an effort to stave off rising anxiety. She simply watched and waited.

Something unfurled in his chest at the realisation that she wasn't asking if he needed help. That she wasn't going to ask.

Cipher waited until he was stable on his legs, at which point she pointed to his radio and said, "Breaking things is always more fun with a soundtrack. We're bringing this."

Not a question but a demand.

Phainon hadn't realised how tense his shoulders were until they began to relax. He huffed, "Yeah, whatever, I don't care."

With a snap of her fingers the radio disappeared into a void of nothingness. The sound emitted by it remained - the broadcast had since moved on to a speculative report on the death of several star systems beyond Hevelius-197 - but the radio was nowhere to be seen. An interesting move on Trickery's behalf. Simultaneously, Cipher was both tricking and solidifying his grasp of reality, keeping his senses rooted in reality while ridding them of the need to physically bring his radio with them to do so.

How interesting trickery could be. He hadn't used the coreflame as much as the others. When his strength returned, he'd need to search to see what its limitations were. Not to the same extent as with Orynyx's coreflames to turn back time - he had clearly learned his lesson and continued to learn it, even after all these weeks. Trickery's foundation was in fooling reality, after all. Use too much and reality bends in a way that couldn't be predicted. It had the potential to cause a lot more trouble than turning back time. If one tricked reality successfully with enough power, the applications were limitless.

"Oh! I think I can hear footsteps." Cipher drew him from his thoughts, cheerful and lighthearted. "We best be off before your little prince and our princess homebody come and ruin all of our fun."

She said that but she hadn't immediately whisked them away with the coin of whimsy. Instead, Cipher's gaze settled onto him, awaiting his final verdict. Waiting for a more explicit 'yes, let's go make shit decisions'. One last opportunity for him to turn her down if he so desired it.

…Phainon really did not want to spend the rest of the day in bed struggling to keep his temper in check. If he had to, then he would be liable to snap and that wouldn't be good for anyone.

And really, he wanted to break things. He did.

"I can hear them too," Phainon said, slowly. "Throw the coin."

Cipher took hold of him and threw the coin.

The world blurred like something out of a kaleidoscopic fever dream. The edges of buildings concaved, the world squished together and reality seemed to blend into itself like a bundle of ink forming a Rorschach blot. The trickery coreflame always made his vision swim whenever it was used in this way - a little like using one of the Trailblaze's waypoints but accompanied by all the added lag of a world struggling to catch up.

Travelling this way used to make him nauseous.

As the cycles had gone on though, much like everything else, Phainon got used to it. Now, all he felt as they moved was a bout of dizziness. And even that was more a symptom of his body's current weakness than that of the trickery coreflame itself.

"Looking a little pale, pretty boy," Cipher sang, and snatched the coin from the air.

The world solidified. It felt a little like gravity and motion was snapping at their heels, richocheting back into place like the return of a rubber band that had been pulled taut before being let go. Phainon stumbled back on shaky legs, remaining on his feet only because Cipher was holding him up. Bright colours still danced at the back of his eyelids in the aftermath of their movement.

…Alright, maybe the coin still affected him when he wasn't at his best. If he wasn't sustaining himself off of the coreflames and was in the habit of eating, Phainon was pretty sure he'd have thrown up all over Cipher's boots.

"Waypoints are better," he groaned.

"Waypoints are boooring," Cipher said. "And so much slower. They're inconvenient. Chasing gold is so much better."

…She said it like the coin of whimsy was made of gold. It was not.

Phainon huffed out a sigh. As the dizziness began to fade he turned to take in his surroundings and tried to figure out what exactly it was that they were here to destroy.

They had moved outside of Okhema. Having travelled past the western entrance to the city, they now stood within a field that had been decimated during the fight with Irontomb. Fire - his flames - had razed the earth and left it inhospitable to any signs of life. There would be no more farming in this spot. Not for a long time.

Since it was no longer a place for growth, it had been repurposed as a waste site.

While not containing the entirety of the rubble and debris from Okhema's streets, the scorched field housed a large percentage of it. Piles of broken roof tiles had been tossed alongside half broken pottery. Crumbling pillars had been rolled into place beside scraps of fabric and snapped children's toys. Anything that had been deemed 'too broken' had been brought to this place and left to be dealt with at a later time.

Phainon's gaze locked on to a half-burnt droma plushie, stuffing pushing free from the gap in its body like spilled organs. His lips pulled into a grimace.

"Everything here is already broken," he said, blankly, as Cipher let him go and stepped out of his personal space. "You said we were going to break things but they're already broken."

When he looked over his shoulder to her, Cipher's brow quirked. "Is that a problem?"

He… wasn't sure.

If he was thinking about it properly, there was a certain satisfaction that came from breaking something that was in one piece versus something that was in multiple. It was going too far to say that it was more interesting but there was a certain amusement to be found in watching something go from being perfectly intact to decimated.

…You just didn't care about damaged things as much. Damaged housewares got thrown away. Damaged buildings got demolished. Damaged people—

Phainon cleared his throat. "I don't know."

"Well, think about it this way," Cipher said, "that mural was in pieces but it still felt pretty fucking good to destroy it even further, right?"

Right.

Yes. That had felt good even if the mural had already been ruled unable to be repaired.

"Yeah," he agreed.

"So, what's the difference?" Cipher asked.

When she put it that way, he supposed that there wasn't one. Not really. His expectations were being subverted but they were still being met. In some ways erasing ruined things could be seen as therapeutic. No more eye-sores. Only that which was functional would remain.

It didn't quite scratch that itch at the depths of his core but that was alright. Delving into such primal parts of himself probably wasn't the best idea anyway. The last time he'd gotten truly lost in that primal side of himself he'd destroyed Aedes Elysiae. He didn't want to do something like that again.

"For the sake of right now," he said, "I suppose there isn't one."

A smirk curled Cipher's lips. "Perfect."

Casting his gaze back to the field, Phainon found that he wasn't entirely sure how to start. If he wanted to be efficient then he could simply tear open space and let everything be consumed within a black hole. But that also seemed too impersonal for something like this. Too quick. It wasn't destruction so much as it was erasure.

"Oh, let me guess what that look means," Cipher said, stalking closer. She pressed a fist to her lips, as if deep in thought, before grinning toothily. "There's no point if it's not fun, right? That's what you're thinking?"

He wasn't justifying that with an answer. Phainon simply waited for her to continue.

"Not indulging me, huh? Oh, you're no fun." She sighed. "Okay, fine. No foreplay wanted in this little situation, I've got it. Here - you'll want to use this."

And with a click of her fingers and a burst of technicolor sparks, her outstretched hand went from holding nothing to holding a bat.

Phainon blinked.

Yep. That was definitely a bat.

It was a glossy shade of obsidian lined with swirling gold curves. The handle was indented with carvings, a series of chimera faces and kitten paws.

"It's not quite Grey Mystery's one," Cipher said, as she held it out. "Trust me, I tried nabbing it, but that girl's got some sort of anti-theft magic going on via path space that means she's able to re-summon it no matter how many times I relocate it into my pockets. I'm not going to lie - I reckon it's rude of her. She should just let me take it. Here. Take it."

Hesitant, Phainon reached for the weapon. Compared to Dawnmaker it was weightless. Even weak as he currently was it felt like he was holding air.

"It's a trickery exclusive," Cipher said. "What do you think?"

As a weapon, it didn't suit him. Beating things to death via blunt force trauma hadn't ever held much appeal. He was much more suited to a blade. Hacking and slicing.

Holding something that didn't suit him as far as weaponry went however… it was probably for the best.

He glanced at the hilt again and said, "…The chimeras are cute."

"Our pretty boy has good taste," Cipher said and scooped down to retrieve a sorry excuse for a jug that was missing it's handle. It also had a long crack running from spout to base. "Here. Aim for a home-run, alright?"

Phainon did not know what a home-run was but when Cipher tossed the jug into the air he assumed it meant that she wanted him to swing.

So he did.

The jug exploded. Shards rained onto dirt like a hailstorm. A thin coat of dust lingered by the bat, much slower in its fall to the earth.

"Good?" Cipher asked.

Phainon nodded. "Good."

"Again?" Cipher asked, lifting another nod with a warped lip that had half melted in the blaze. He lifted his bat in anticipation. "Time to let loose. I've got a whole pile of these bad boys for us to get through."

The last time Phainon fully let loose, he lost an arm, two wings and fought God. It was not necessarily the best idea for him to do that again. Letting loose only a little would have to do.

It was easy to distract himself with broken ceramics. Jugs and plates shattered in a way that brought satisfaction no matter how heavy hitting the swing. It was almost understandable why Stelle always went around swinging her own bat. Phainon could get used to using one.

…Thinking of Stelle, he really did have to call her back on his teleslate soon. He'd been avoiding her messages ever since she'd told him of the Geniuses and while he wasn't willing to tell her about his upcoming trip to Styxia, he didn't want to ignore her completely. She was Amphoreus' saviour. His saviour.

"Hey, pretty boy," Cipher said, when their current pile of crockery had been dwindled into dust and shards too small to shatter further with the swing of a bat. "Do you… like Amphoreus?"

Huh?

His surprise must've slipped free because Cipher tilted her head and said, "Indulge me a little before we start on the glassware. Do you?"

Phainon's hold of the bat tightened. Voice flat, he said, "I went through everything for Amphoreus. I love it."

Loved it.

Cipher wagged a finger, clicking her tongue. "Nuh-uh. That's not answering what I was asked."

"…Amphoreus is my home."

"But," she said, forcefully. "Do you like it?"

Why was she asking?

Why?

The words were torn from his throat as if she'd reached inside of him and scraped them free with her claws. Voice raw, Phainon grit out, "…No."

And then, because he had already started and the admission couldn't be taken back: "No. I don't. I hate it here. It's— It's hell. I thought the Era Nova was supposed to be better but I still hate it here."

Something akin to shame started to climb up each notch of his larynx, as if trying to tear itself free from the depths of his rotting soul. He should've liked Amphoreus, shouldn't he? Should've loved the coastline and the people and the very earth that he'd spent so many years protecting.

But he didn't.

Sometimes, thinking of Amphoreus made his skin crawl. While others celebrated the planet's emergence alongside the wider galaxy all Phainon felt was nauseous. They had sacrificed everything time and time again, and that was great for everyone else. All he felt was a net loss. After everything, the end result didn't really feel worth it.

Cipher nodded as if she'd been expecting the words.

"Too many shitty memories?" She asked.

The shame was taking up too much space in his mouth to speak so instead, Phainon dipped his head in a small nod. His hair fell over his eyes and though he knew Cipher was still watching him, it offered a degree of separation from the conversation that lessened the roiling sickness that had begun coalescing in his stomach.

"Thought so," Cipher said. "I get like that with Okhema. A little distance always helps."

"That's part of why we're going to Styxia," Phainon said, slowly.

"But that's not really getting distance, is it?" she asked. Her voice shifted into something more contemplative. It felt strange to hear the tone, compared to her typical mischievous drawl. "It gets you away from Okhema but you've probably got shitty memories all over the planet. Is going to Styxia going to help?"

His brows furrowed. "Well it's not like anywhere else is going to be any better. Styxia is— it's better than being here."

"Oh wow, a minimal passing grade." The return to a drawl was more sarcastic than mischievous. Pointed. As if waiting for him to get the point. "Just what I've always wanted. A pile of shit that's just a tiny bit better than the shit I'm already stuck with."

His jaw clenched. His fingernails dug into the bat with enough force that he heard the wood splinter. "Don't."

Raising her hands in surrender, Cipher said, "Okay, okay. All I'm trying to say is that if you need distance from Amphoreus, why aren't you leaving?"

The question was simple and yet it made his thoughts quieten.

He'd never considered leaving Amphoreus before. In part because there was always a need for the Eternal Recurrence to continue that required his ongoing presence. But even without the weight of the cycles on his shoulders, the space beyond the sky wasn't meant for Amphoreans. They were just code, after all.

…They might not be coded people anymore. But it still wasn't possible.

It wasn't.

"I can't just leave Amphoreus."

Cipher scrunched her brows to almost comical proportions. It made it difficult to take her seriously. Perhaps that was purposeful though - instead of getting angry and lashing out, he was bordering more on dismissive. "Why not?"

"Amphoreus needs me."

"Amphoreus can survive long enough for you to take a trip."

"It's my home—"

"—That you don't even like. And either way, people leave home all the time. I did. You did. This time it'll even be here when you want to come back."

Phainon heaved a sigh from his nose. Air whistled from his nostrils like a warning flare.

"Maybe if I had wings, I'd be able to just leave but I don't have wings. The only way off this planet right now is via the Astral Express and that's not going to happen. Styxia is the best option I've got."

One of Cipher's ears twitched. Then, they both perked up. Her tail followed suit as a grin transformed her lips. It was the sort of look that she had before stealing an expensive gemstone or some ancient relic promised to sell for extortionate amounts.

"You've got it all wrong pretty boy," she said. "You've got all those Trickery coreflames inside you. With enough belief, travel past the skies will be a breeze. You just need a decent base to build your trick from."

She paused. Whether to gauge his interest or for dramatic effect, it was difficult to say. He waited, not sure whether he was interested or not. Phainon was certainly sceptical, at least.

"Lucky for you," Cipher finally said, which made him think that the pause really was for dramatic effect after all. "I've got the perfect idea for your base." She lifted the coin of Whimsy. "You don't need to commit but there's no reason not to check it out, right?"

"What's the idea?"

"You were partially right when you said the Nameless were the only ones who could get you off Amphoreus right now." Cipher said, rolling the coin between her fingers. "Grey mystery got here in one of those train cars, right? We just need to go back to the crash site and use it."
